sources.title: Doshi-Velez, Kim: Towards A Rigorous Science of Interpretable Machine Learning (arXiv:1702.08608)
sources.access: web open (curl -sSL abs page and PDF, HTTP 200; PDF converted with pdftotext and read section by section)
claims: Defines interpretability as the ability to explain or to present in understandable terms to a human

Need for interpretability stems from incompleteness of the problem formalization (safety, ethics, mismatched objectives); systems with no significant consequences or that are well validated may not need explanation
Three-level evaluation taxonomy: application-grounded, human-grounded, functionally-grounded

sources.title: Lipton: The Mythos of Model Interpretability (arXiv:1606.03490, ICML 2016 WHI workshop)
sources.access: web open (curl -sSL abs page and PDF, HTTP 200; PDF converted with pdftotext and read section by section)
claims: Interpretability has no formal technical meaning and is not a monolithic concept; motivations (trust, causality, transferability, informativeness, fair decisions) are diverse and occasionally discordant
Splits properties into transparency (simulatability, decomposability, algorithmic transparency) and post-hoc interpretability (text, visualization, local explanations, explanation by example)
Questions the claim that linear models are always more interpretable than deep networks; high-dimensional linear models lose simulatability

sources.title: Rudin: Stop Explaining Black Box Machine Learning Models for High Stakes Decisions and Use Interpretable Models Instead (arXiv:1811.10154, Nature Machine Intelligence 2019)
sources.access: web open (curl -sSL abs page and PDF, HTTP 200; PDF converted with pdftotext and read section by section)
claims: Distinguishes explaining black boxes with a second post-hoc model (Explainable ML) from inherently interpretable models
Interpretability is domain-specific; no all-purpose definition
Inherently interpretable models give explanations faithful to what the model computes; argues the accuracy-interpretability trade-off is often a myth for data with meaningful features

sources.title: NIST AI 100-1: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0), section 3.5
claims: Explainability is a representation of the mechanisms underlying AI operation and answers 'how'; interpretability is the meaning of output in the context of designed purpose and answers 'why'
Published January 2023

sources.title: NISTIR 8312: Four Principles of Explainable Artificial Intelligence
claims: Four principles: explanation, meaningful, explanation accuracy, knowledge limits (September 2021)
Explanation accuracy is distinct from decision accuracy
Meaningful principle: explanations understandable to the intended consumer; developers and end users have different needs

claims: SHAP values are Shapley values; they explain how to get from the base value (expected prediction with no features known) to the current output
Theorem 1: within additive feature attribution methods, only one solution satisfies local accuracy, missingness and consistency
Exact computation is challenging; approximations may assume feature independence and model linearity

claims: Three deliberately speculative claims: features correspond to directions; features connected by weights form circuits (computational subgraphs); universality
Polysemantic neuron in InceptionV1 responds to cat faces, fronts of cars and cat legs

sources.title: Templeton et al. (Anthropic): Scaling Monosemanticity (Transformer Circuits Thread, 2024)
sources.access: web open (curl -sSL, HTTP 200; HTML tags stripped and read section by section)
claims: Setting: sparse autoencoders on middle-layer residual stream activations of Anthropic's medium-sized production model; three SAEs of about 1M, 4M and 34M features; reconstruction explains at least 65% of variance
Features are multilingual and multimodal; clamping the Golden Gate Bridge feature to 10x its maximum activation makes the model self-identify as the bridge

Limitations: far from all features found, likely orders of magnitude short even for the middle layer; features for only about 60% of London boroughs in the 34M SAE; training objective is a proxy for interpretability
Caution: knowing about lies, being able to lie and actually lying differ; hope for interpretability as a 'test set for safety' is very preliminary

sources.title: Jacovi, Goldberg: Towards Faithfully Interpretable NLP Systems: How should we define and evaluate faithfulness? (arXiv:2004.03685, ACL 2020)
sources.access: web open (curl -sSL abs page and PDF, HTTP 200; PDF converted with pdftotext and read section by section)
claims: Plausibility is how convincing an interpretation is to humans; faithfulness is how accurately it reflects the model's true reasoning process; one can hold without the other
Faithfulness evaluation should not rely on human judgement

claims: Model parameter randomization test compares saliency on a trained model with a randomly initialized network of the same architecture

sources.title: Slack et al.: Fooling LIME and SHAP: Adversarial Attacks on Post hoc Explanation Methods (arXiv:1911.02508, AIES 2020)
sources.access: web open (curl -sSL abs page and PDF, HTTP 200; PDF converted with pdftotext and read section by section)
claims: Scaffolding hides a perfectly discriminatory classifier that uses only the sensitive feature (race for COMPAS and Communities and Crime, gender for German credit) by detecting perturbation samples

LIME fooled on all three datasets; SHAP shifts importance away from the sensitive feature on most data points (84% COMPAS, 100% CC, 85% German with one uncorrelated feature; 67% and 71% for COMPAS and CC with two)
